headline: At six levels the split is total: the styled perf runtime holds 0.671 ms/1k where the 9.6.0 baseline hits 5.26 (7.8×), and the css-prop fold ships one 2.66 kB class that ties `vanilla` while `panda`'s inline `css()` reaches 18.5 ms/1k.

microbench.why: The css-prop fold merges six levels into one className at 0.508 ms/1k, tying `vanilla` (0.509). The styled perf runtime collapses six `Yak` renders into one component and holds 0.671 ms/1k, where the 9.6.0 baseline renders all six and reaches 5.26 ms/1k, a 7.8× gap. `panda`'s inline `css()` runs its serializer six times per element at 18.5 ms/1k, the case's slowest; the hashers 1.47-3.11.

autocannon.why: The single-class fold serves 1544 req/s with `vanilla` (1517); the styled perf runtime 1219. The 9.6.0 baseline collapses to 181 as six wrappers render per request, `panda`'s css-fn to 52.0.

attribution.why: At six levels `vanilla` renders in 0.595 ms; the styled perf runtime's flat 0.138 ms library slice puts it at 0.698 ms, a hair ahead of the css-prop fold (0.780 ms, library 0.137) whose single long concatenated class costs a little more to emit here. The 9.6.0 baseline pays 3.65 ms of library time for six nested `Yak` renders (5.19 ms total); `panda`'s css-fn 19.9 ms of component self-time (22.8 ms).

hydrate.why: The folded paths hydrate near `vanilla` at 46.7-49.9 ms. The css-prop 9.7 twin regresses to 90.9 ms here, an artifact of its component tree at depth; the styled perf runtime hydrates cleanly at 49.9 ms. Runtime hashers inject and reflow, `styled-components` 101 ms, `emotion` 120 ms.

inp.why: Re-rendering a six-level subtree costs ~6.60-7.60 ms across the static-class lanes with `styled-components` and `cnfast` in front. The 9.6.0 baseline reaches 24.2 ms, `goober` 22.6, `panda`'s css-fn 58.5 ms.

mount.why: Cold mount lands at 70.4-74.5 ms for the folded paths and `vanilla`; the css-prop fold leads and, unlike its one- and three-level figures, sits in the normal cluster here. The 9.6.0 baseline 99.2 ms, the hashers 99-151 ms.

renderTiming.why: One recalc per lane at any depth; the browser's style pass is unaffected by composition.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships one class no matter the depth, 2.66 kB gzipped, under `vanilla` (3.08 kB) and unchanged from `compose-1`; the styled perf runtime 4.04 kB. The 9.6.0 baseline barely differs (4.05 kB) since the cost is CPU; `StyleX` 5.86 kB, the hashers 15-16 kB.

nsweep.why: At 4000 six-level trees the css-prop fold holds 2.15 ms near `vanilla` (2.06); the styled perf runtime 2.66 ms. The 9.6.0 baseline explodes to 21.6 ms (8.1× the perf runtime) and `panda`'s css-fn to 75.1 ms, the depth tax at full scale.

crossCase: The deep end of the composition ladder (`compose-1`, `compose-3` above). Six levels is where the perf runtime earns its default: 0.671 ms/1k against the 9.6.0 baseline's 5.26 (7.8×), while its library slice stays flat at 0.138 ms. The css-prop fold's one concatenated class holds `vanilla`'s render cost and its 2.66 kB payload at every depth.
